import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.17

by L. A. Kurdachenko

Let $G$ be an $FC$-group whose derived subgroup is embeddable in a direct product of finite
groups. Must $G/Z(G)$ also be embeddable in a direct product of finite groups?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.17»

/-- A group is an $FC$-group if every conjugacy class is finite. -/
def IsFCGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, (conjugatesOf g).Finite

/-- A group is residually finite if every nonidentity element remains nonidentity under some
homomorphism to a finite group. Equivalently, it embeds in a direct product of finite groups. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 →
    ∃ (F : Type) (_ : Group F) (_ : Finite F) (f : G →* F), f g ≠ 1

/--
Let $G$ be an $FC$-group and suppose its derived subgroup $G'$ is embeddable in a direct
product of finite groups. Must $G/Z(G)$ be embeddable in a direct product of finite groups?
Equivalently, does residual finiteness of $G'$ imply residual finiteness of $G/Z(G)$ for every
$FC$-group $G$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.17» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsFCGroup G → IsResiduallyFinite (commutator G) →
      IsResiduallyFinite (G ⧸ Subgroup.center G) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.17»
modeling_decisions: Interpreted an FC-group as a group for which `conjugatesOf g` is a finite set for every element `g`.

Used the standard element-separation characterization of residual finiteness for “embeddable in an unrestricted direct product of finite groups”: every nonidentity element has nonidentity image under some homomorphism to a finite group.
Represented the derived subgroup by Mathlib's `commutator G` subgroup type and represented `G/Z(G)` by `G ⧸ Subgroup.center G`.
Followed the repository's yes/no convention by placing the universally quantified implication on the right side of `answer(sorry) ↔ ...`.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.17

by L. A. Kurdachenko

(M. J. Tomkinson). Let $G$ be an $FC$-group whose derived subgroup is embeddable in a
direct product of finite groups. Must $G/Z(G)$ be embeddable in a direct product of finite
groups?

An $FC$-group is a group in which every conjugacy class is finite. As usual in the theory of
$FC$-groups (P. Hall, Tomkinson), "direct product" means the *restricted* direct product: the
subgroup of the Cartesian product consisting of the elements with only finitely many
nontrivial coordinates. (Embeddability in an unrestricted Cartesian product of finite groups
is just residual finiteness, and $G/Z(G)$ is residually finite for every $FC$-group $G$ by a
classical theorem of Baer, so that reading would make the question trivial.)

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 10.17
- M. J. Tomkinson, *FC-groups*, Research Notes in Mathematics 96, Pitman, 1984
-/

open scoped RestrictedProduct

namespace Kourovka.«10.17»

universe u

/-- A group $G$ is an *$FC$-group* if every conjugacy class of $G$ is finite. -/
def IsFCGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ c : ConjClasses G, c.carrier.Finite

/-- A group $H$ is *embeddable in a direct product of finite groups* if there is an injective
group homomorphism from $H$ into the restricted direct product
$$\mathrm{Dr}_{i \in I} F_i = \{ (x_i) \in \prod_{i \in I} F_i :
  x_i = 1 \text{ for all but finitely many } i \}$$
of a family $(F_i)_{i \in I}$ of finite groups. In Lean this is the restricted product
`Πʳ i, [F i, ⊥]` of the `F i` with respect to the trivial subgroups and the cofinite filter. -/
def IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups (H : Type u) [Group H] : Prop :=
  ∃ (ι : Type u) (F : ι → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, Group (F i)) (_ : ∀ i, Finite (F i))
    (φ : H →* Πʳ i, [F i, (⊥ : Subgroup (F i))]), Function.Injective φ

/-- Every finite group is an $FC$-group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFCGroup.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsFCGroup G :=
  fun c ↦ c.carrier.toFinite

/-- Every abelian group is an $FC$-group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFCGroup.of_commGroup (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] : IsFCGroup G := by
  intro c
  obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ := ConjClasses.mk_surjective c
  refine (Set.finite_singleton a).subset fun x hx ↦ ?_
  rw [ConjClasses.mem_carrier_iff_mk_eq, ConjClasses.mk_eq_mk_iff_isConj, isConj_iff_eq] at hx
  exact hx

/-- Every finite group is embeddable in a direct product of finite groups. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups.of_finite (H : Type u) [Group H] [Finite H] :
    IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups H := by
  refine ⟨PUnit, fun _ ↦ H, inferInstance, inferInstance,
    { toFun := fun h ↦ ⟨fun _ ↦ h, by simp [Filter.cofinite_eq_bot]⟩
      map_one' := rfl
      map_mul' := fun _ _ ↦ rfl }, fun x y hxy ↦ ?_⟩
  exact congrArg (fun z : Πʳ _ : PUnit, [H, (⊥ : Subgroup H)] ↦ z PUnit.unit) hxy

/--
(M. J. Tomkinson). Let $G$ be an $FC$-group whose derived subgroup $G'$ is embeddable in a
direct product of finite groups. Must $G/Z(G)$ be embeddable in a direct product of finite
groups?

Here "direct product" is the restricted direct product, as is standard in the theory of
$FC$-groups.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.17» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsFCGroup G →
      IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups (commutator G) →
      IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups (G ⧸ Subgroup.center G) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.17»
attempts.decomposition_objections: The table's note glosses "embeddable in a direct product of finite groups" as embeddability in an unrestricted (Cartesian) product, i.e. residual finiteness. I believe this is wrong and did not follow it. (1) In the FC-group literature (P. Hall, Tomkinson's monograph "FC-groups", Robinson) "direct product" (Dr) is the restricted direct product, while the unrestricted one is called the "Cartesian product" (Cr); Tomkinson's question is posed in that terminology. (2) Under the Cartesian reading the question is trivial and hypothesis-free: for any FC-group G, each C_G(g^G) is a normal subgroup of finite index (finite intersection of the finite-index centralizers of the finitely many conjugates of g) and their intersection is Z(G), so G/Z(G) embeds in the Cartesian product ∏_g G/C_G(g^G) of finite groups — the classical theorem of Baer that G/Z(G) is residually finite for every FC-group. A problem trivially answered in 1948 would not be listed as open in the 2024 edition. (3) Restricted embeddability is genuinely stronger than residual finiteness (e.g. a torsion-complete abelian p-group is a residually finite periodic FC-group that is not a subgroup of a restricted direct product of finite groups, by Kulikov's theorem), so the two readings give different statements and only the restricted one is a non-trivial open question. The slot name and text span were followed exactly; only the interpretive note was overridden.
modeling_decisions: "Direct product of finite groups" is modelled as the RESTRICTED direct product (Mathlib `RestrictedProduct` with the cofinite filter and trivial subgroups, `Πʳ i, [F i, (⊥ : Subgroup (F i))]`), not the Cartesian product / residual finiteness; see decomposition_objections for the justification.
FC-group is defined as `∀ c : ConjClasses G, c.carrier.Finite` (every conjugacy class is a finite set); equivalent alternatives (finite ConjAct-orbits, finite-index centralizers) were not used.

`IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups (H : Type u)` quantifies over index types `ι : Type u` and finite groups `F : ι → Type u` in the same universe as `H`. This is without loss of generality: one may shrink the index set to the coordinates actually hit by H (cardinality ≤ |H|·ℵ₀) and replace each finite group by an equivalent copy on `Fin n`.
The universally quantified group `G` lives in `Type` (as in the other Kourovka files), so both `↥(commutator G)` and `G ⧸ Subgroup.center G` are in `Type` and the definition is used at universe 0.

The derived subgroup is `commutator G = ⁅⊤, ⊤⁆`, coerced to a type with its subgroup `Group` structure; the center is `Subgroup.center G` and the quotient `G ⧸ Subgroup.center G` uses Mathlib's normality instance for the center.

Three short `@[category API]` lemmas (finite groups and abelian groups are FC; finite groups are embeddable) are included as basic tests of the bespoke definitions, per CONTRIBUTING.md; they are fully proved.

Mathlib supplies `commutator G` (derived subgroup), `Subgroup.center`, the quotient group, `ConjClasses.carrier`, and `RestrictedProduct` (`Πʳ i, [F i, ⊥]`, the restricted direct product); two bespoke predicates (FC-group; embeddability in a restricted direct product of finite groups) were needed since neither exists in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib.

by L. A. Kurdachenko

(M. J. Tomkinson). Let $G$ be an $FC$-group whose derived subgroup is embeddable in a
direct product of finite groups. Must $G/Z(G)$ be embeddable in a direct product of finite
groups?

An $FC$-group is a group in which every conjugacy class is finite. Following the notebook's

question would be void: for every $FC$-group $G$, the quotient $G/Z(G)$ embeds in the
Cartesian product of the finite groups $G/C_G(x^G)$, $x \in G$.)

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.17»

universe u

/-- A group `G` is an $FC$-group if every conjugacy class of `G` is finite. -/
def IsFCGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, (ConjClasses.mk g).carrier.Finite

/-- A group `G` is embeddable in a direct product of finite groups if there is an injective group
homomorphism from `G` into a Cartesian product `∀ i, F i` of finite groups `F i` all of whose
values have finite support, i.e. lie in the restricted direct product of the `F i`. -/
def IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFinite (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (ι : Type u) (F : ι → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, Group (F i)) (_ : ∀ i, Finite (F i))
    (f : G →* ∀ i, F i), Function.Injective f ∧ ∀ g : G, {i | f g i ≠ 1}.Finite

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFCGroup_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsFCGroup G :=
  fun _ => Set.toFinite _

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFinite_of_finite (G : Type u) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFinite G :=
  ⟨PUnit, fun _ => G, inferInstance, inferInstance, Pi.constMonoidHom PUnit G,
    fun _ _ h => congrFun h PUnit.unit, fun _ => Set.toFinite _⟩

/--
(M. J. Tomkinson). Let $G$ be an $FC$-group whose derived subgroup $G'$ is embeddable in a
(restricted) direct product of finite groups. Must $G/Z(G)$ be embeddable in a (restricted)
direct product of finite groups?
-/

    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsFCGroup G →

attempts.decomposition_objections: The notes gloss "embeddable in a direct product of finite groups" as embeddable in an UNRESTRICTED (Cartesian) product, i.e. residually finite. I believe this is wrong. In the Kourovka Notebook's (and Tomkinson's book "FC-groups") terminology, the direct product (Dr) of an infinite family is the restricted one, while the unrestricted one is the Cartesian product (Cr). Decisively: under the Cartesian/residually-finite reading the question is trivially answered "yes" with no hypothesis on G' at all — for any FC-group G and x ∈ G, N_x := ⋂_{y ∈ x^G} C_G(y) is a normal subgroup of finite index (finite intersection of finite-index centralizers) and ⋂_x N_x = Z(G), so G/Z(G) ↪ ∏_x G/N_x, a Cartesian product of finite groups. This is a standard textbook fact (Tomkinson, FC-groups, Ch. 1), so Tomkinson's open question must concern the restricted direct product (which additionally forces, e.g., periodicity). I therefore formalized the restricted-direct-product reading and did not use residual finiteness; the slot name, text span, quantifier structure and answer(sorry) idiom conform to the table.
modeling_decisions: "Direct product of finite groups" is read as the RESTRICTED direct product (finitely supported elements of ∏ F_i), following the notebook's/Tomkinson's terminology; the Cartesian (residually finite) reading would make the question trivially true (see decomposition_objections). The module docstring explains this briefly.

IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFinite (G : Type u) quantifies over ι : Type u and F : ι → Type u. Since the theorem takes G : Type, index types and factors live in Type. This is WLOG: only the union of the (finite) supports of the images matters, which has cardinality ≤ max(|G|, ℵ₀), and finite groups are small.
The restricted product is encoded directly (injective hom G →* ∀ i, F i with {i | f g i ≠ 1} finite for all g) rather than via Mathlib's RestrictedProduct, for transparency; the two are equivalent.
FC-group is encoded as finiteness of every conjugacy class (ConjClasses.mk g).carrier, which is the literal definition (equivalently, every centralizer has finite index).
Derived subgroup is Mathlib's `commutator G` (= ⁅⊤, ⊤⁆), taken as a group via the subtype coercion; G/Z(G) is `G ⧸ Subgroup.center G`.

Two small proven @[category test] lemmas (finite groups are FC-groups and are embeddable in a direct product of finite groups) are included as basic API tests for the bespoke definitions, as CONTRIBUTING.md requests.

of the Cartesian product $\prod_{i \in I} F_i$ consisting of the elements with only finitely many
non-trivial coordinates. This convention is essential: $G/Z(G)$ embeds in the Cartesian product
$\prod_{x \in G} G/C_G(x^G)$ of finite groups for every $FC$-group $G$, so for unrestricted
products the question would have a trivial positive answer.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

universe u

namespace Kourovka.«10.17»

/-- A group $G$ is an $FC$-group if every conjugacy class of $G$ is finite. -/
def IsFCGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, (conjugatesOf g).Finite

/-- A group $H$ is embeddable in a direct product of finite groups if there are finite groups
$F_i$, $i \in I$, and an injective homomorphism from $H$ into the Cartesian product
$\prod_{i \in I} F_i$ whose image lies in the restricted direct product $\mathrm{Dr}_{i \in I} F_i$,
that is, every element of the image has only finitely many non-trivial coordinates. -/
def IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups (H : Type u) [Group H] : Prop :=
  ∃ (ι : Type u) (F : ι → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, Group (F i)) (_ : ∀ i, Finite (F i))
    (f : H →* ∀ i, F i), Function.Injective f ∧ ∀ h : H, {i | f h i ≠ 1}.Finite

/-- Every finite group is an $FC$-group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsFCGroup.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsFCGroup G :=
  fun _ => Set.toFinite _

/-- Every abelian group is an $FC$-group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsFCGroup.of_commGroup (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] : IsFCGroup G := by
  intro g
  have : conjugatesOf g = {g} := by
    ext x
    simp [conjugatesOf, isConj_iff_eq, eq_comm]
  rw [this]
  exact Set.finite_singleton g

/-- Every finite group is embeddable in a direct product of finite groups. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups.of_finite (G : Type u) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups G :=
  ⟨PUnit, fun _ => G, inferInstance, inferInstance, Pi.monoidHom fun _ => MonoidHom.id G,
    fun _ _ h => congrFun h PUnit.unit, fun _ => Set.toFinite _⟩

/--
(M. J. Tomkinson). Let $G$ be an $FC$-group whose derived subgroup $G'$ is embeddable in a direct
product of finite groups. Must $G/Z(G)$ be embeddable in a direct product of finite groups?

Here "direct product" is the restricted direct product $\mathrm{Dr}_{i \in I} F_i$, as is standard
in the theory of $FC$-groups.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.17» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsFCGroup G →
      IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups (commutator G) →
      IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups (G ⧸ Subgroup.center G) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.17»
attempts.decomposition_objections: The slot notes assert that "embeddable in a direct product of finite groups" means embeddable in an unrestricted (Cartesian) product of finite groups, i.e. residually finite. This reading is wrong for this problem. For every FC-group G, Z(G) = ⋂_x C_G(x^G) is an intersection of finite-index normal subgroups (each conjugacy class x^G is finite, so its centralizer has finite index), hence G/Z(G) embeds in the Cartesian product ∏_x G/C_G(x^G) of finite groups. So under the Cartesian reading the answer is trivially "yes" for every FC-group, the hypothesis on G' is irrelevant, and the problem would not be open. In the FC-group literature (Tomkinson, "FC-groups", 1984; Robinson's convention Dr vs Cr) "direct product" means the restricted direct product (elements with finitely many non-trivial coordinates), and this is the reading under which the question (the converse of Tomkinson's theorem that G/Z(G) ∈ Dr-embeddable ⇒ G' Dr-embeddable) is non-trivial and open. I formalized the restricted-direct-product reading and did not follow the notes' residual-finiteness reading, since a faithful statement of the open problem cannot be trivially true.
modeling_decisions: "Direct product of finite groups" is modelled as the restricted direct product: an injective hom f : H →* ∀ i, F i into a product of finite groups such that every f h has finite support {i | f h i ≠ 1}. This deviates from the decomposition notes (Cartesian product / residually finite), which would trivialize the problem; see decomposition_objections.
FC-group is modelled as ∀ g, (conjugatesOf g).Finite, i.e. every conjugacy class is finite (Mathlib's conjugatesOf g = {b | IsConj g b}).
Derived subgroup is Mathlib's `commutator G` (= ⁅⊤, ⊤⁆) and Z(G) is `Subgroup.center G`; G/Z(G) is `G ⧸ Subgroup.center G`.

G is quantified over `Type` (universe 0), as in the sibling Kourovka files; the index type and factors of the direct product live in the same universe as H. This loses nothing: the union of the supports of the image elements has cardinality ≤ max(|H|, ℵ₀), so any embedding can be re-indexed within the same universe.
Finite groups F i are given by `Finite (F i)`; the index type is arbitrary (possibly empty, in which case only the trivial group embeds).

The module docstring and theorem docstring state the restricted-product convention explicitly and briefly explain why it is essential (Cartesian reading is trivial). Three `category test` API theorems with complete proofs are included for the bespoke definitions (finite groups are FC, abelian groups are FC, finite groups embed in a direct product of finite groups).

/-!
# Conjecture 10.17

by L. A. Kurdachenko

(M. J. Tomkinson). Let $G$ be an $FC$-group whose derived subgroup is embeddable in a
direct product of finite groups. Must $G/Z(G)$ be embeddable in a direct product of finite
groups?

An $FC$-group is a group in which every element has only finitely many conjugates. Following
the conventions of the Kourovka Notebook and of Tomkinson's monograph *FC-groups*, the direct
product $\mathrm{Dr}_{i \in I} F_i$ of a family of groups is the restricted direct product:
the subgroup of the Cartesian product $\mathrm{Cr}_{i \in I} F_i = \prod_{i \in I} F_i$
consisting of the elements with only finitely many non-identity coordinates. (Embeddability in
a Cartesian product of finite groups would be the weaker property of residual finiteness.)

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.17»

/-- A group is an $FC$-group if every conjugacy class is finite. -/
def IsFCGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, (conjugatesOf g).Finite

/-- A group $G$ is embeddable in a direct product of finite groups if there is an injective
group homomorphism from $G$ into the Cartesian product $\prod_{i \in I} F_i$ of a family of
finite groups $F_i$ whose image consists of elements of finite support, i.e. lies in the
(restricted) direct product $\mathrm{Dr}_{i \in I} F_i$. -/
def IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (ι : Type) (F : ι → Type) (_ : ∀ i, Group (F i)) (_ : ∀ i, Finite (F i))
    (f : G →* ∀ i, F i), Function.Injective f ∧ ∀ g : G, {i | f g i ≠ 1}.Finite

/-- Every finite group is an $FC$-group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFCGroup.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsFCGroup G :=
  fun _ => Set.toFinite _

/-- Every finite group is embeddable in a direct product of finite groups. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups.of_finite (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups G :=
  ⟨Unit, fun _ => G, fun _ => inferInstance, fun _ => inferInstance,
    { toFun := fun g _ => g, map_one' := rfl, map_mul' := fun _ _ => rfl },
    fun _ _ h => congrFun h (), fun _ => Set.toFinite _⟩

/--
(M. J. Tomkinson). Let $G$ be an $FC$-group whose derived subgroup $G'$ is embeddable in a
direct product of finite groups. Must $G/Z(G)$ be embeddable in a direct product of finite
groups?

Here "direct product" is the restricted direct product, as in the Kourovka Notebook and in
Tomkinson's book *FC-groups*; see `IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.17» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsFCGroup G →
      IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups (commutator G) →
      IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups (G ⧸ Subgroup.center G) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.17»
attempts.decomposition_objections: The table's note asserts that "embeddable in a direct product of finite groups" means embeddable in an unrestricted (Cartesian) product, hence residual finiteness. I believe this is a misreading. (1) The Kourovka Notebook (Novosibirsk school; Kargapolov–Merzlyakov conventions) and M. J. Tomkinson's monograph "FC-groups" (Robinson's Dr/Cr notation) both distinguish the *direct product* Dr (restricted: finitely supported elements) from the *Cartesian product* Cr (unrestricted); "subgroup of a direct product of finite groups" is a named class in Tomkinson's book, strictly smaller than the residually finite groups even among periodic FC-groups (P. Hall: for countable periodic FC-groups the two coincide; Gorčakov gave an uncountable residually finite periodic FC-group not embeddable in a Dr of finite groups). (2) The notebook uses the phrase "residually finite" freely elsewhere; had that been meant, the problem would say so. (3) The proposer L. A. Kurdachenko's own research programme concerns FC-groups embeddable in direct products (Dr) of finite groups (and an abelian group), so the wording is his technical term. I therefore formalized the literal statement with the restricted direct product and documented this in the module and theorem docstrings. Note the two readings agree for countable G (by P. Hall's theorem, since G' and G/Z(G) are periodic FC-groups); they differ only for uncountable G. I did not add the residually-finite reading as a variant theorem because I cannot vouch for its open/solved status.
modeling_decisions: 'Direct product' of an infinite family of finite groups is taken to be the restricted direct product (elements of finite support), per Kourovka/Tomkinson conventions; the decomposition note's Cartesian/residually-finite reading was deliberately not followed (see objections).

Embeddability is expressed as: ∃ ι : Type, F : ι → Type, [∀ i, Group (F i)], [∀ i, Finite (F i)], an injective MonoidHom f : G →* ∀ i, F i with {i | f g i ≠ 1}.Finite for every g. Restricting ι and F i to the universe Type loses no generality: finite groups have copies in Type, and a group in Dr F_i also embeds in the Dr of its finite quotients G/ker(π_i), indexed by a set of subgroups of G.
FC-group is defined as: every conjugacy class conjugatesOf g is finite (equivalently every centralizer has finite index).
The quantification is over G : Type, matching the other Kourovka files (1_40, 19_25, 20_76).
The derived subgroup is Mathlib's commutator G (= ⁅⊤, ⊤⁆), used as a type via the subgroup coercion; G/Z(G) is G ⧸ Subgroup.center G.

Two small API lemmas with complete proofs (finite groups are FC-groups and are embeddable in a direct product of finite groups) are included as sanity checks for the bespoke definitions, tagged category API, AMS 20.
